findings.title: retry.md: Blockquote continuation marker changed from `-` to `>`
findings.evidence: Line 95 changed from `-` to `>` (blockquote continuation marker)
findings.why: The diff shows line 95 changing from a dash continuation `-` to `>` continuation for a multiline blockquote. This is a minor markdown formatting inconsistency correction, not a semantic change.
findings.recommendation: Accept — this normalizes blockquote syntax (a `>` blockquote continuation is more standard than a bare `-` in most markdown parsers).

findings.title: Node.js 16+ inconsistency across mcp-servers.md
findings.evidence: Tavily changed to Node.js 18+ at line 149, but other servers (context7, playwright, twentyfirst, morph, serena) remain at Node.js 16+ (lines 48, 63, 78, 93, 108, 172). Line 316 also still says 'need v16+'.
findings.why: The PR adopts Tavily 0.2.x which requires Node 18+, but leaves inconsistency: the doc now has mixed Node version requirements (16+ for most servers, 18+ for Tavily/Auggie). Line 316's troubleshooting section still says 'need v16+' which is now insufficient for the Tavily/Auggie servers documented above it.
findings.recommendation: Document whether Node 16+ is the global minimum or per-server. If 18+ is now required globally (because Tavily/Auggie are high-priority), update line 316 and consider a note that some servers need 18+. If 16+ remains valid for most servers, the current state is acceptable but line 316 could be clarified ('need v16+ minimum; some servers require v18+').

findings.title: comprehensive-features.md: tavily.json deletion listed but file was not in visible config tree
findings.evidence: Line 125 in the diff removes `- tavily.json` from a list, implying it was previously documented as part of the config files. Test `test_tavily_json_absent` in tests/cli/test_install_mcp_tavily.py:40-43 confirms the deleted path was `src/superclaude/mcp/configs/tavily.json`.
findings.why: The PR claims the orphan config was deleted in Phase 2 (X2), and the test confirms this. However, the list context in comprehensive-features.md is unclear — the deletion appears in a section that previously listed example config files, but the actual location (mcp/configs/) is not visible in the surrounding lines. This is likely correct cleanup of a stale reference, but without seeing the full original list context it's hard to confirm the claim is grounded.
findings.recommendation: Verify the deleted tavily.json reference was in the correct section (looks like it was in a config file list). The deletion is correct per X2 and the test.

findings.title: No test guards X5 confinement for brainstorm/troubleshoot/reflect skills
findings.evidence: test_tier2_tool_id_parity (line 28) checks that brainstorm/troubleshoot/reflect skills do NOT reference tavily-extract/map/crawl (X5). However, the test only covers troubleshoot-protocol and reflect-protocol (via _ALL_FOUR). The diff also changes sc-brainstorm-protocol/SKILL.md but test_tier2_tavily_consistency.py does not explicitly include brainstorm in its _ALL_FOUR list (lines 15-20 define _TROUBLESHOOT_CMD, _TROUBLESHOOT_SKILL, _REFLECT_CMD, _REFLECT_SKILL only).
findings.why: The PR's invariant X5 claims map/crawl are confined to deep-research ONLY, meaning brainstorm/troubleshoot/reflect must NOT gain them. The test file test_tier2_tavily_consistency.py has a _FORBIDDEN_TOOLS check but only tests troubleshoot and reflect files, not brainstorm. The test_rf_no_map_crawl in test_tavily_tool_parity.py checks rf-* agents only (line 82-89), which does not cover the brainstorm skill. There appears to be a gap: sc-brainstorm-protocol is changed in the diff but not explicitly tested for X5 confinement.
findings.recommendation: Verify sc-brainstorm-protocol/SKILL.md does not introduce map/crawl references (manual inspection confirmed it does not). Consider extending test_tier2_tavily_consistency.py to include brainstorm in _ALL_FOUR or adding a separate test for brainstorm X5 confinement.

findings.title: X7 frontmatter↔prose parity: deep-research-agent.md and deep-research.md both declare 4 Tavily tools correctly
findings.evidence: Frontmatter tools: list (lines 6-9) declares all 4: tavily-search, tavily-extract, tavily-map, tavily-crawl. Prose references all 4 with full IDs in Discovery Routing section (lines 212-217). deep-research.md frontmatter (lines 6-9) also declares all 4, and prose references them in Discovery Routing (lines 42-48). Test test_documenting_files_have_exact_parity guards this (tests/agents/test_tavily_tool_parity.py:62).
findings.why: The PR claims exact frontmatter↔prose parity (invariant X7). Both agent files correctly add tavily-map and tavily-crawl to frontmatter AND reference them in prose with full mcp__tavily__tavily-* IDs. The test confirms this parity is enforced.
findings.recommendation: Accept — X7 holds for deep-research agents.

findings.evidence: All changes are `line_number:` field updates (+1 shift for 3 entries in mcp-servers.md, +1 shift for 6 entries in install_mcp.py). No new `hashed_secret` values introduced. `generated_at` timestamp updated to 2026-06-23T17:31:33Z.

cross_cutting_observations.title: X5 confinement claim is correctly implemented but test coverage has a gap
cross_cutting_observations.why: The PR claims map/crawl are confined to the deep-research engine (X5), meaning brainstorm/troubleshoot/reflect must NOT reference them. Manual inspection confirms: troubleshoot-protocol only references tavily-search (line 335, 510), reflect-protocol only references tavily-search (line 1690), and brainstorm-protocol only references tavily-search indirectly via '/sc:research' delegation (line 636) with no tool IDs listed. However, the test file test_tier2_tavily_consistency.py only covers troubleshoot and reflect (not brainstorm). The broader test_tavily_tool_parity.py:test_rf_no_map_crawl only covers rf-* agents. There is no explicit test asserting sc-brainstorm-protocol does not reference map/crawl.
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Extend test_tier2_tavily_consistency.py to include sc-brainstorm-protocol in the _ALL_FOUR check, or add a dedicated test for brainstorm X5 confinement. The implementation is correct, but the test gap leaves the invariant partially unguarded.

cross_cutting_observations.title: MCP_Tavily.md is correctly positioned as canonical 0.2.x surface with pointer architecture
cross_cutting_observations.why: The PR claims MCP_Tavily.md is the canonical reference and other docs point to it rather than restating the surface. Evidence: MCP_Tavily.md:5 states 'This file is the canonical Tavily capability reference; other docs point here rather than restating the surface.' RESEARCH_CONFIG.md:61 says 'pinned — see the install_mcp.py registry and MCP_Tavily.md'. FLAGS.md:72 says 'see MCP_Tavily.md'. comprehensive-features.md:117 says 'see MCP_Tavily.md'. mcp-servers.md:146 says 'see MCP_Tavily.md'. Test test_docs_no_default_params_duplication (tests/docs/test_tavily_doc_alignment.py:97) confirms docs/ does not duplicate DEFAULT_PARAMETERS values.
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Accept — pointer architecture is correctly implemented and tested.

cross_cutting_observations.title: DEFAULT_PARAMETERS baseline and per-call override (X3/M4) are correctly documented and tested
cross_cutting_observations.why: The PR documents the server-level DEFAULT_PARAMETERS baseline (search_depth: basic, max_results: 10) in install_mcp.py:85 and MCP_Tavily.md:61-66, and the intentional per-call override for troubleshoot Tier-2 (search_depth: advanced) in MCP_Tavily.md:68-80 and troubleshoot-protocol/SKILL.md:335. Test test_default_parameters_field (line 34) confirms the registry field. Test test_default_parameters_propagated (line 71) confirms the install argv carries the DEFAULT_PARAMETERS env var. Test test_troubleshoot_search_depth_advanced (line 56) confirms troubleshoot names the override and reflect does not. The X3 split is correctly implemented and the M4 exception is documented as intentional.
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Accept — DEFAULT_PARAMETERS mechanics are correctly implemented, documented, and tested.

notes_for_orchestrator: Seven findings total: 1 trivial markdown style fix (retry.md blockquote), 1 low-severity Node version inconsistency (mcp-servers.md), 1 low-severity config list context question (comprehensive-features.md), 1 medium-severity test gap (brainstorm X5 not explicitly tested), and 3 clean/positive confirmations (X7 parity, version pin, .secrets.baseline). Three cross-cutting observations confirm X5 implementation (with test gap noted), canonical MCP_Tavily.md pointer architecture, and DEFAULT_PARAMETERS mechanics. No contradictions, no real secrets, no X5 violations in prose. The test gap for sc-brainstorm-protocol is the only substantive process issue — the implementation is correct but the invariant is not fully guarded by tests.
